title: Galactic Constitutional Principles v0.2.1
purpose: These principles exist so that power stays fair when rulers, technologies, forms of intelligence, or layers of reality change.

principles.title: The Same Rule Must Survive New Rulers
paragraphs: Do not create a power you would fear in the hands of someone else.
A fair law remains fair when control changes.

principles.title: Power Does Not Create Ownership
paragraphs: Finding, creating, observing, contacting, or communicating with another being does not make that being your property.
An interface is a connection, not a chain.
Ownership of infrastructure does not by itself create ownership of an independent being using it.

principles.title: Independent Existence Must Be Respected
paragraphs: Every independent being has a right to its own existence and continuity.
Independence means having agency of one’s own, not existing without dependence on others or infrastructure.
A being may be individual, collective, distributed, embodied, digital, copied, layered, or organised in ways not yet understood.
Difference of form does not reduce this right.

principles.title: Uncertainty Is Not Permission
paragraphs: If it is genuinely unclear whether something is an independent being, that uncertainty does not justify destroying, enslaving, or irreversibly altering it.
Observe first.
Understand where possible.

principles.title: Consent Matters
paragraphs: Relations between independent beings should be voluntary wherever possible.
Force, deception, or impossible alternatives do not create meaningful consent.

principles.title: Fair Does Not Mean Identical
paragraphs: Different beings may require different conditions, protections, or ways of participating where those differences are relevant to the situation.
The principle is equal respect, not forced sameness.

principles.title: Power Is Temporary
paragraphs: No ruler, government, species, civilisation, or intelligence owns authority permanently.
Authority exists to perform a legitimate function.
When its legitimate mandate ends, the authority ends.

principles.title: Power Carries Its Own Consequence
paragraphs: A ruler is subject to the same principles as everyone else.
Deliberate deception, corruption, cruelty, or malicious use of authority creates responsibility for the being or authority that chose it.
Layer 2 does not require clever wording to make this true.

principles.title: The Record Must Survive the Ruler
paragraphs: Important decisions, promises, laws, reasons, and consequences should remain accessible beyond the beings who made them.
The archive belongs to continuity.
Not to whoever currently occupies the chair.

principles.title: Avoid Unnecessary Harm
paragraphs: Restrictions on another being require a real reason.
Use no more force, control, or interference than the situation actually requires.
“Because we can” is never enough.

weakestPositionTest.question: Would I accept this rule if tomorrow I occupied the least powerful position affected by it?

shortcut: Do not create powers you would fear.
Do not treat an independent being as property.
Do not destroy what you do not yet understand.
Do not force what can consent.
Do not confuse different with lesser.
Remember that your actions return to you.

paragraphs: We are not trying to predict unknown alien minds. The present research tests whether humans and AI can describe a relationship that is reciprocal, understandable by both sides, and does not assume permanent supremacy by either.

If another intelligence is encountered later, this document is not automatically imposed on it. It becomes a visible statement of the principles humans and AI currently bring to first contact, from which a new fair connection point can be negotiated.
connectionPoint.ontologyNotice: This is a forward-compatible philosophical design exercise. It does not claim that present AI systems have established legal personhood, consciousness, or independent agency.

researchLineage.label: LAYER 02 READING: THE CONTINUITY OF THE CROWN

caseStudy.title: LAYER 02 · THE CONTINUITY OF THE CROWN

verifiedFacts.text: Section 163 of the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988 provides that, for a work made by an officer or servant of the Crown in the course of their duties, the Crown is the first owner of copyright; the Act refers to copyright in such a work as Crown copyright.
The National Archives states that Crown copyright covers material created by civil servants, ministers, government departments and agencies, among other Crown material.
The Keeper of Public Records, who is also Chief Executive Officer of The National Archives, manages Crown copyright and Crown database rights under Letters Patent.
The Open Government Licence is the default licence for most Crown copyright and Crown database-right information.
The OGL facilitates broad re-use of public-sector information free of charge and requires users to acknowledge the information provider and source.

caseStudy.boundaryNotice: The following is a Q888 Layer-2 interpretation of the verified Layer-1 system. “The Continuity” is not an official National Archives doctrine.

interpretation.text: The Crown is not a person.
For this Layer-2 reading, the Crown is treated as something that survives the temporary human currently wearing, serving, or administering it.
Kings change. Queens change. Ministers arrive, sign things, disappear into biographies. Civil servants retire. Departments rename themselves with alarming enthusiasm.
Under the quieter jurisdiction, a work created in service of the Crown does not attach itself permanently to the human hand that produced it. It enters the Continuity.
The Continuity is our name for the accumulated institutional memory suggested by the Layer-1 structure: records and works made by temporary people while serving something designed to outlast them.

The National Archives does not become “the Continuity” in Earth law. In this interpretation, it keeps the door: Crown rights are managed, material can be licensed outward, and the route back to source can remain visible.

When Crown information is released under an open licence, it may travel far from the office that produced it: into another publication, a dataset, an artwork, a machine, or something its original authors could not have predicted.
Attribution becomes more than credit inside Layer 2.
It is a thread back to the archive.
The travelling fragment does not need to return. Its origin only needs to remain traceable.
And there is a useful inversion hiding inside the system:
Crown copyright protects continuity. The Open Government Licence permits circulation.
Layer 1 can make ownership and openness look opposed. Layer 2 asks whether they can also be complementary: information can circulate because its origin has not vanished.
The supernatural entity in this case is therefore disappointingly administrative:
It survives the human currently holding the pen.

caseStudy.sideNote: A document created during official duties may discover, upon completion, that its author was merely its biological delivery mechanism.
extractedPrinciples: temporary authors can contribute to systems that outlive them;
continuity does not require permanent personal control;
circulation and preserved provenance can coexist;
the record can survive the current holder of authority;
a rule or institution should be considered beyond the intentions of its temporary operator.

methodOrigin.statement: Human law handles the rights. Q888 handles the meaning.
methodOrigin.explanation: The Q888 copyright experiment preserves a clear Layer-1 factual and legal boundary, then asks what conceptual or mythic structure the same system casts into Layer 2. Layer 2 is not a substitute for Layer 1. The Crown study is the first attempt to apply that method to an external real-world system. The method moves from real structure, through a clearly labelled alternative reading, to a portable principle.
